boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named stops along Bismarck’s Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail, the Riverfront Trail corridor connecting cultural, historical, and recreational sites beside the Missouri River.

cards.title: Walk the interpretive village trail
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor
cards.notes: Start at the overlook and follow the 0.55-mile interpretive trail to read about the Mandan earth-lodge village once located here.
cards.short_summary: An archaeological overlook with an interpretive walking trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks lists Chief Looking’s Village as an earth-lodge village occupied about 1550–1600, with a 0.55-mile unpaved interpretive trail.
cards.source_title: Chief Looking's Village — Bismarck Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Gate is open daily May–October, weather depending; the park page lists hours of 8:00am–10:00pm.

cards.title: Pause at Sonali’s Garden
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Chief Looking’s Village
cards.notes: Include the garden during an overlook visit, then continue on the connecting trail toward the Riverfront Trail and Pioneer Park.
cards.short_summary: A named garden within the Chief Looking’s Village destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks lists Sonali’s Garden among the features at Chief Looking’s Village, which connects to the Riverfront Trail.
cards.source_title: Chief Looking's Village — Bismarck Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: The park page notes a weather-dependent daily gate opening from May through October.

cards.title: Follow the river trail through Pioneer Park
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, 1500 River Rd.
cards.notes: Use Pioneer Park as a Riverfront Trail stop for its paved shared-use route, public art, playground, and river-adjacent grounds.
cards.short_summary: A River Road park that combines trail access and public art.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks lists Pioneer Park at 1500 River Rd. with the paved shared-use Riverfront Trail, a playground, public art, and a keelboat replica.
cards.access_notes: Bismarck Parks lists park hours of 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: Read the keelboat signage
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Pioneer Park
cards.notes: Find the replica keelboat in Pioneer Park and use its interpretive signage to add a focused history stop to a river-trail walk.
cards.short_summary: A relocated Lewis and Clark Bicentennial keelboat replica.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks says Pioneer Park has a keelboat replica with interpretive signage and that the replica was relocated there in 2025.
cards.access_notes: Located within Pioneer Park, whose listed hours are 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: Locate the Rising Eagle sculpture
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Pioneer Park
cards.notes: Use the park’s public-art listing to find Rising Eagle, then continue along the paved Riverfront Trail toward the next river stop.
cards.short_summary: One of the Eagle Sculpture Series works in Pioneer Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks identifies Rising Eagle as part of its Eagle Sculpture Series and places it at Pioneer Park.
cards.source_title: Public Art & Culture — Bismarck Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Pioneer Park is listed at 1500 River Rd. and open 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: See the riverbank steamboat replica
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, 1970 River Road
cards.notes: Stop at the four-acre riverbank park to view the steamboat replica and interpretive signs before rejoining the paved shared-use trail.
cards.short_summary: A compact River Road stop with a steamboat replica.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks says Steamboat Park at 1970 River Road has a steamboat replica, interpretive signs, and the paved Riverfront Trail.
cards.access_notes: Bismarck Parks lists park hours of 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: Find Reflections by the river
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Steamboat Park
cards.notes: Pair the eagle sculpture with the nearby replica steamboat, then follow the river corridor south toward Sertoma Park at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: An Eagle Sculpture Series work at Steamboat Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks lists Reflections in its Eagle Sculpture Series at Steamboat Park, 1970 River Road.
cards.source_title: Public Art & Culture — Bismarck Parks & Recreation

cards.title: Take the Bill Mills Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, 300 Riverside Park Rd.
cards.notes: At the north end of Sertoma Park, take the 0.8-mile unpaved Bill Mills Nature Trail for interpretive panels and Missouri River views.
cards.short_summary: A large Riverfront Trail park with a short interpretive nature trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks lists Sertoma Park at 300 Riverside Park Rd. and identifies the 0.8-mile Bill Mills Nature Trail with interpretive panels and river views.
cards.access_notes: Sertoma Park’s page lists hours of 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: View Gathering of Visions
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Sertoma Park
cards.notes: Look for Gathering of Visions near the Dakota Zoo entrance and use the public-art description to understand the mosaic eagle work’s context.
cards.short_summary: A 2005 Eagle Sculpture Series work near the zoo entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks places Gathering of Visions at Sertoma Park near the Dakota Zoo entrance and records its dedication on November 18, 2005.
cards.source_title: Public Art & Culture — Bismarck Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Sertoma Park is at 300 Riverside Park Road; listed park hours are 6:00am–11:00pm.

cards.title: Finish at The Keeper
cards.subtitle: Missouri Valley Millennium Legacy Trail (Riverfront Trail) corridor, Sertoma Park
cards.notes: Head toward Shelter 9 to locate The Keeper, then use it as a final public-art stop before leaving the Riverfront Trail corridor.
cards.short_summary: A named Eagle Sculpture Series work near Sertoma Park Shelter 9.
cards.evidence_claim: Bismarck Parks places The Keeper at Sertoma Park near Shelter 9 and records its dedication on September 4, 2008.
cards.source_title: Public Art & Culture — Bismarck Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Sertoma Park is at 300 Riverside Park Road; listed park hours are 6:00am–11:00pm.
